articles.title: Donald Trump's million-dollar gift to his assistant, Natalie Harp, is shaking the walls of the White House
articles.standfirst: Natalie Harp, Margo Martin, and Chamberlain Harris received a large sum of money
articles.summary: Natalie Harp, Margo Martin, and Chamberlain Harris received a large sum of money
articles.body:
The amounts appear in the financial disclosures of the three advisers, recently released by the U.S. Administration . In the documents, Donald Trump appears as the person who made the payments, described as a “cash gift for the holidays”.

The figure is especially striking because of its size. Each of the three aides receives an annual salary close to $150,000 for her work in the White House , so the money received as a gift is approximately equivalent to 30% of her annual salary.

Donald Trump gave a total of $135,000 in cash to three of his closest aides at the White House . The beneficiaries, Natalie Harp , Margo Martin and Chamberlain Harris, stated that they had each received $45,000 from the U.S. president, payments that have raised doubts among ethics experts about their possible legal standing.

Trump and the doubts about the legality of the payments: the “gift” amounts to 30% of their salaries

The payments have sparked controversy because U.S. federal legislation places restrictions on the additional compensation that public employees may receive beyond their official salary.

Natalie Harp , 35, is the best known of the three. Her closeness to Trump has on several occasions placed her at the center of media attention. Margo Martin , 31, works as a communications adviser and usually accompanies the president to record content for his social media.

The third beneficiary is Chamberlain Harris , 26, who serves as the executive assistant to the president and is also part of his innermost circle.

But those were not the only amounts handed over. According to information published by U.S. media, Trump also allegedly gave $20,000 to Walt Nauta, director of operations for the Oval Office and the president's former personal aide.

Experts consulted by the American press say they do not recall similar public precedents in which a president had handed such large amounts of cash to White House employees. A case that once again puts the internal practices of Trump’s closest circle under the spotlight.

articles.title: Savannah Guthrie’s choice of words about missing mom Nancy raises questions
articles.standfirst: Savannah’s brief on-air remark comes seven months after Nancy Guthrie disappeared from her Arizona home
articles.summary: Savannah’s brief on-air remark comes seven months after Nancy Guthrie disappeared from her Arizona home
articles.body:
Savannah Guthrie made a poignant reference to her missing mother, Nancy Guthrie , during Thursday’s episode of Today, seven months after the 84-year-old disappeared from her Arizona home.

The NBC anchor was discussing an upcoming Today trip to Ireland when she briefly spoke about her family’s heritage. Savannah explained that her mother was Irish and that her maternal grandmother’s family came from Galway.

The simple comment carried extra emotional weight because Savannah referred to Nancy in the past tense.

“My mother’s family w-, my mother was Irish, her grandmother,” said Savannah . “They were from Galway.”

The moment came as Savannah and her fellow hosts celebrated plans for the entire Today team to broadcast live from Ireland on October 16. Savannah said she’d never visited the country and appeared excited about finally making the trip.

While she maintained her usual upbeat demeanor, the wording quickly attracted attention given the circumstances surrounding her mother’s disappearance.

A source has denied that Savannah’s use of the past tense was intended to confirm that Nancy has died. Authorities, meanwhile, continue to investigate Nancy’s disappearance as an active case.

The FBI says Nancy was last seen at her Tucson residence on January 31, 2026, and investigators are seeking information that could help locate her or identify those responsible.

Savannah Guthrie continues to seek answers

Nancy’s disappearance has left Savannah and her siblings facing an agonizing period of uncertainty. Investigators have released surveillance footage showing an armed individual appearing to tamper with a camera at Nancy’s front door around the time she vanished.

The FBI and Pima County Sheriff’s Department have continued working together on the investigation.

Savannah has previously acknowledged that her mother may no longer be alive. In August, she marked the passage of six months with an emotional social media message, describing the family’s pain while continuing to plead for information.

She wrote that the family wakes each day trying to remain strong, drawing on the resilience Nancy taught them. At the same time, Savannah made clear that the family’s grief hasn’t diminished their determination to discover what happened.

The Guthrie family has also offered a $1 million reward for information leading to Nancy’s return, while the FBI is offering up to $50,000 for information leading to her recovery or the arrest and conviction of anyone involved in her disappearance.

The upcoming Ireland broadcast will therefore carry a meaning beyond television for Savannah . Galway is part of her mother’s family history, making the journey especially significant during such a painful chapter.

The Today team’s Ireland trip was also inspired by a 2025 conversation between Savannah and Irish actor Pierce Brosnan , when she expressed her long-standing desire to visit the country.

Savannah’s latest reference to her mother was brief, but it served as another reminder that the disappearance continues to weigh heavily on her and her family.

articles.title: A buyer’s dream! The cities where home prices are dropping heading into the fall
articles.standfirst: There could be a good investment closer than you think.
articles.summary: There could be a good investment closer than you think.
articles.body:
Summer is nearing its final days and, after a vacation season that had a little bit of everything, fall seems determined not to be left behind. This time, the surprise is coming for those who have been looking to buy a home: home prices are falling in several U.S. cities .

The numbers behind this shift were published by Realtor.com , and they show that the adjustment is not an isolated trend. In August, the median price per square foot of homes for sale fell 1.8% from the same month in 2025 , marking the 10th consecutive month of year-over-year declines.

The difference also becomes clear when the country is broken down by region. The median price per square foot fell 3.6% in the Northeast, 2.6% in the South and 2.1% in the West, while the Midwest saw no change .

And within all of this, one question emerges:

Why are sellers lowering their prices?

The reason comes down to a combination of more homes on the market and still-elevated mortgage rates , a scenario that is giving buyers more options to compare and more room to decide how much they are willing to pay.

Meanwhile, Jake Krimmel, a senior economist at Realtor.com, has pointed out that many of the areas now seeing the biggest declines have something in common: they were among the major cities that experienced a strong housing boom between 2020 and 2022 .

That is prompting some sellers to change their strategy and move closer to the price buyers are actually willing to pay, rather than waiting for the market to once again favor higher prices.

Which cities are seeing the biggest price declines?

Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos, Texas: -8.1%

Tampa-St. Petersburg-Clearwater, Florida: -5.6%

Memphis, Tennessee-Mississippi-Arkansas: -4.1%

San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont, California: -3.9%

San Antonio-New Braunfels, Texas: -3.6%

Denver-Aurora-Centennial, Colorado: -3.4%

Baltimore-Columbia-Towson, Maryland: -3.2%

San Diego-Chula Vista-Carlsbad, California: -2.7%

Orlando-Kissimmee-Sanford, Florida: -2.6%

Portland-Vancouver-Hillsboro, Oregon-Washington: -2.4%

The No. 1 spot stands out considerably from the rest. Austin recorded an 8.1% decline, the steepest drop among the metropolitan areas included in this group.

And while the figures show where the adjustment is happening most sharply, some markets are still telling a completely different story.

Not every city is seeing prices fall

While those markets are recording declines, other cities continue to move in the opposite direction.

Providence, Rhode Island, saw a 9.3% increase in the median price per square foot , while Indianapolis rose 4.4% and Chicago gained 3.6%.

The difference makes one thing clear: there is no single trend across the entire U.S. What a buyer finds can look very different depending on the city and the kind of lifestyle they are looking for.

That difference between markets is precisely what Realtor.com's data shows, rather than pointing to a broad decline across the entire housing market.

articles.title: SSDI Benefits 2027 Changes: What is changing for Social Security disability beneficiaries next year?
articles.standfirst: Disability beneficiaries are expected to receive higher payments, while a feared eligibility overhaul has been abandoned.
articles.summary: Disability beneficiaries are expected to receive higher payments, while a feared eligibility overhaul has been abandoned.
articles.body:
Social Security Disability Insurance beneficiaries are heading into 2027 with one major financial change expected, but without the sweeping eligibility restrictions that had previously worried disability advocates.

The most immediate change will be the annual cost of living adjustment. The exact 2027 COLA won’t be confirmed until October 14, but current estimates are around 3.5%.

For an SSDI recipient receiving the average worker disability benefit of about $1,635 per month, a 3.5% increase would add roughly $57 monthly.

2027 SSDI payments are expected to increase

The COLA is designed to help Social Security payments keep pace with inflation rather than provide beneficiaries with a genuine increase in purchasing power.

"A COLA isn't really a raise; it's catch-up for inflation you already paid," retirement expert Geoffrey Schmidt told Yahoo Finance.

The final percentage could still change because the Social Security Administration calculates the adjustment using inflation data from the third quarter of the year.

Importantly, there are no scheduled cuts to Social Security benefits in 2027 under current law.

"Nothing taking effect in 2027 cuts your benefit or rewrites the rules against you," Schmidt said.

That means SSDI recipients should expect their existing benefit to continue, with the annual COLA applied once the final figure is announced.

Major disability eligibility overhaul has been dropped

Another significant development is something that now won't happen.

The Social Security Administration had considered changing how it evaluates disability claims, including potentially reducing the importance of age when deciding whether applicants can adjust to other work.

Those proposals caused concern that older applicants could find it considerably harder to qualify for SSDI. However, the SSA later told disability advocates it wasn't moving forward with the planned overhaul.

" Social Security Disability Insurance is a critical lifeline for people who find themselves no longer able to work," AARP vice president of financial security Jenn Jones said.

The existing disability evaluation system therefore remains in place rather than being replaced by the previously discussed rules.

For current SSDI beneficiaries , the picture for 2027 is consequently more straightforward than some earlier reports suggested.

Monthly benefits are expected to rise through the COLA, while the major eligibility changes that could have tightened access to disability benefits have been shelved.

articles.title: CPI Inflation Report release: When was it announced this month and how much did inflation increase?
articles.standfirst: The latest CPI report showed inflation accelerating in August, with gasoline prices responsible for a significant part of the monthly rise.
articles.summary: The latest CPI report showed inflation accelerating in August, with gasoline prices responsible for a significant part of the monthly rise.
articles.body:
The latest Consumer Price Index report has now been released, giving Americans a fresh look at inflation and how quickly the cost of everyday goods and services is rising.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics published the August 2026 CPI report at 8:30 a.m. ET on Friday, September 11.

Headline inflation increased 0.4% during August on a seasonally adjusted basis, accelerating sharply from the 0.1% monthly rise recorded in July.

"The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) increased 0.4 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in August after rising 0.1 percent in July," the BLS said.

CPI inflation remained at 3.4% annually

Over the 12 months through August, consumer prices increased 3.4%. That was unchanged from the annual inflation rate recorded in July.

"The all items index rose 3.4 percent for the 12 months ending August as it did for the 12 months ending July," the BLS said.

Core inflation, which removes the more volatile food and energy categories, rose 0.3% during August. On an annual basis, core CPI increased 2.4%, easing from 2.5% in July.

Energy was one of the biggest reasons headline inflation accelerated during the month.

"The index for gasoline rose 3.9 percent in August, accounting for over one third of the monthly all items increase," the BLS said.

Energy prices overall increased 2.1% during August, while shelter costs rose 0.3% and food prices increased 0.1%.

When is the next CPI inflation report?

The September CPI report won't arrive until next month.

According to the official BLS schedule, September 2026 inflation figures will be released on Wednesday, October 14, at 8:30 a.m. ET.

That report will attract particular attention because inflation remains above the Federal Reserve's long-term 2% target and consumer prices continue to influence expectations for interest rates.

It will also provide the final piece of third-quarter CPI-W data needed to calculate the 2027 Social Security cost-of-living adjustment.

For September, however, the key number is now confirmed: consumer prices rose 0.4% in August and were 3.4% higher than they were a year earlier.

articles.title: How is Social Security Disability Benefits calculated? This is how your earnings determine what you receive
articles.standfirst: SSDI payments are based mainly on your work history and past earnings, not on how severe Social Security considers your disability to be.
articles.summary: SSDI payments are based mainly on your work history and past earnings, not on how severe Social Security considers your disability to be.
articles.body:
Social Security Disability Insurance benefits aren't calculated using a fixed payment for each type of disability. Instead, the Social Security Administration looks at your earnings record and works out how much you paid into the system during your working years.

The first step is calculating your Average Indexed Monthly Earnings , known as AIME. Social Security adjusts previous earnings to account for changes in national wage levels and then uses the relevant years from your work history to produce a monthly average.

Your disability itself doesn't determine the payment amount once you qualify. Two people with the same medical condition can receive very different SSDI benefits because their earnings histories are different.

How Social Security turns earnings into an SSDI payment

Once Social Security has calculated your AIME, it uses that figure to determine your Primary Insurance Amount, or PIA.

For somebody who first becomes eligible for disability benefits in 2026, the formula applies 90% to the first $1,286 of AIME, 32% to earnings between $1,286 and $7,749, and 15% to any amount above $7,749.

Those amounts are then added together to produce the PIA, which forms the basis of the worker's monthly disability benefit.

The percentages remain fixed, but the dollar thresholds, known as bend points, are adjusted over time in line with changes in national wages.

Why your SSDI benefit can be different from someone else's

The amount ultimately depends on how much you earned in jobs covered by Social Security and how long you worked before becoming disabled.

A worker with consistently higher covered earnings will generally receive a larger SSDI payment than somebody with a lower earnings history.

The average monthly benefit for disabled workers in 2026 is about $1,630, but individual payments can be considerably higher or lower.

Other factors can also affect what is actually paid. Certain public disability benefits, including some workers' compensation payments, can reduce SSDI, while eligible spouses or children may qualify for additional benefits based on the worker's record.

The easiest way to see a personalized estimate is through a my Social Security account, which uses your actual earnings record.

The central rule is simple: SSDI eligibility depends on both medical and work requirements, but the size of your monthly benefit is primarily determined by your past Social Security covered earnings.

articles.title: The United States puts a 32-hour workweek on the table: working less while maintaining current pay
articles.standfirst: The proposal seeks to progressively reduce the weekly working hours
articles.summary: The proposal seeks to progressively reduce the weekly working hours
articles.body:
The four-day workweek is gaining ground again in the United States. A group of lawmakers has brought to Congress a proposal that aims to change one of the most established rules of the U.S. labor market: the 40-hour workweek as the benchmark for starting to count overtime.

The initiative proposes reducing that limit to 32 hours . And there is one especially striking detail: the reduction in working hours should not translate into a pay cut for workers. In other words, the idea would be to work fewer hours while keeping the same pay.

Change would not come all at once

The project, driven by Senator Bernie Sanders and Congressman Mark Takano, envisions a gradual transition until reaching 32 hours per week . The intention is for companies to have enough leeway to adapt their schedules and organization.

One of the main changes would occur in the calculation of overtime hours. Currently, workers begin to accrue overtime once they exceed 40 hours per week. Under the new proposal, that threshold would be set at 32.

For an employee used to an eight-hour workday over five days, the change could be as simple as eliminating one workday. In other cases, companies might choose to distribute those hours differently throughout the week.

Supporters of the measure believe that working less can have positive effects on rest and productivity . The idea is that an employee who arrives at work less tired can make better use of the hours they spend there. It also aims to reduce the strain associated with overly long working days.

But the proposal faces a complicated debate ahead. For many companies, maintaining wages while reducing hours means increasing the real cost of each hour worked. The impact could be especially significant for businesses that need to maintain continuous service and depend on shifts.

Furthermore, the fact that the proposal has reached Congress does not mean that it will automatically become law . It would still have to go through the entire U.S. legislative process.

articles.title: US Consumer Price Index Prediction: How much is inflation expected to rise and what will it mean for COLA?
articles.standfirst: The latest inflation figures have strengthened expectations for a larger Social Security cost of living adjustment in 2027.
articles.summary: The latest inflation figures have strengthened expectations for a larger Social Security cost of living adjustment in 2027.
articles.body:
US inflation remains one of the most important numbers for millions of Americans, particularly Social Security recipients waiting to learn how much their benefits could increase next year.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics released the August Consumer Price Index on September 11. Headline inflation rose 0.4% during the month and was 3.4% higher than a year earlier.

Trading Economics had expected the CPI index to rise to around 334.9 points, compared with 333.92 previously, while its broader third-quarter forecast points to annual inflation of about 3.7%.

The next major reading will be September inflation, which will complete the three-month period used to calculate the 2027 Social Security COLA.

What is predicted for US inflation?

Trading Economics expects inflation to remain elevated through the third quarter before easing later.

Its current projections put annual inflation at around 3.7% for the third quarter of 2026 before falling toward 3.4% by the end of the year.

Monthly inflation is also projected to remain positive, meaning prices are still expected to rise even if the annual rate eventually begins to cool.

The September CPI report will be particularly important because it will provide the final data needed for Social Security's annual adjustment.

What could inflation mean for the 2027 COLA?

Social Security doesn't calculate COLA using the headline CPI figure most commonly reported in the news.

Instead, the calculation uses the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, known as CPI W, and compares the average reading from July, August, and September with the same three-month average from the previous year.

After the August inflation report, estimates for the 2027 COLA are generally sitting between about 3.4% and 3.6%.

That would be higher than the 2.8% adjustment beneficiaries received for 2026.

The final figure remains unknown because September's CPI-W reading hasn't yet been released.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics is scheduled to publish September inflation data on October 14, after which the Social Security Administration can announce the official 2027 COLA.

Until then, persistent inflation suggests beneficiaries are likely to receive a noticeably larger adjustment next year, although the exact percentage will depend on the final September figures.

articles.title: Social Security COLA Increase 2027: What is the latest projection with August's U.S. inflation?
articles.standfirst: Fresh inflation data has pushed the leading 2027 Social Security COLA estimates into the mid-3% range, but beneficiaries will have to wait until October for the official figure
articles.summary: Fresh inflation data has pushed the leading 2027 Social Security COLA estimates into the mid-3% range, but beneficiaries will have to wait until October for the official figure
articles.body:
S ocial Security recipients have received a clearer indication of how much their benefits could increase next year after the latest U.S. inflation figures were released, with current forecasts pointing to a 2027 cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) of around 3.5% to 3.6%.

The latest estimate from AARP puts the potential increase at 3.6%, while the Senior Citizens League (TSCL) is projecting a slightly lower 3.5% adjustment. Both forecasts are above the 2.8% COLA that beneficiaries received for 2026.

The projections come as the government releases the final pieces of inflation data needed to calculate next year's increase. August's figures showed that consumer prices remained elevated, reinforcing expectations that Social Security payments will receive a larger adjustment in 2027.

According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers increased 3.4% over the 12 months through August.

Prices climbed 0.4% on a seasonally adjusted basis during the month, while the energy index rose 2.1%. Gasoline prices increased 3.9% in August and were 27.4% higher than a year earlier.

The inflation measure used specifically for the Social Security calculation, however, is the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, or CPI-W. The CPI-W increased 3.5% over the 12 months through August, according to the BLS.

That distinction is important because the annual Social Security COLA is not simply based on the headline inflation rate reported each month.

How August inflation affects the 2027 COLA

The Social Security Administration calculates the COLA using the average CPI-W readings for July, August and September and compares that three-month average with the corresponding period from the previous year. September's number is therefore the final piece of the calculation.

AARP's latest forecast of 3.6% uses the available inflation data through August, together with a projection for September. The organization says the estimate would add approximately $75 to the average retired worker's monthly benefit.

The Senior Citizens League is slightly more conservative, forecasting a 3.5% increase. Its estimate has moved down from 3.6% previously, illustrating why the final percentage cannot yet be treated as certain.

If the 3.6% forecast ultimately becomes reality, an average monthly retirement benefit of around $2,086 would rise by approximately $75 per month.

A 3.5% increase would produce a somewhat smaller boost. AARP notes that the exact dollar increase will vary depending on the individual's current benefit amount.

The 2027 adjustment would also represent a noticeable increase compared with this year's 2.8% COLA . However, a larger check does not necessarily mean beneficiaries will experience a substantial improvement in their purchasing power.

Inflation has continued to affect several categories that are particularly important to older Americans.

The August BLS report showed food prices were up 2.7% from a year earlier, while shelter increased 3.0%. Medical care rose 1.6%, and energy prices were up 16.3% over the same period.

Those figures help explain why some retirees may feel that even a mid-3% Social Security increase will not fully compensate for their expenses.

AARP's Rich Johnson said current data provides a solid basis for the estimate, while emphasizing that September could still alter the final calculation.

“With only one month of inflation data to go until the 2027 COLA is finalized, there’s less uncertainty about what that increase will be,” he said. “Unless prices change dramatically in September, we’re confident that the COLA will be in the mid-3 percent range.”

The official number is expected on October 14, 2026, when the September inflation data is released and the SSA completes its calculation. The resulting adjustment will apply to Social Security benefits beginning in January 2027.

For now, the latest evidence suggests beneficiaries should prepare for a COLA somewhere around 3.5% to 3.6%, with 3.6% currently representing AARP's leading estimate. But until September's CPI-W data is available, the final 2027 Social Security increase remains subject to change.

articles.title: This is Elon Musk's 100-billion-dollar base to conquer space: Starbase Louisiana
articles.standfirst: Its construction will begin in 2027 and the first launch is scheduled for 2029
articles.summary: Its construction will begin in 2027 and the first launch is scheduled for 2029
articles.body:
Elon Musk sets his sights on space. The richest man in the world ($892 billion in net worth according to Forbes magazine) regularly insists on the need to obtain energy beyond Earth and to colonize the Moon or Mars . To do so, the CEO of SpaceX has designed Starbase Louisiana , a gigantic base whose construction will begin in 2027 and whose aim is to drive space conquest forward. The first spacecraft launch, according to the company itself, is scheduled for 2029 .

Starbase Louisiana will cost $100 billion

'Elon Musk's latest major project, Starbase Louisiana , will cost at least 100 billion dollars . SpaceX, the company responsible for the ambitious project, promises that the facilities will employ more than 3,000 people , prioritizing the hiring of the nearby population. The goal is, according to what they have reported, for the United States to remain at the forefront of the space race. "It will be built to support thousands of Starship flights per year ," they explain.'

This will be Starbase Louisiana: its location and its gigantic size

Starbase Louisiana will be located in the Pacanera , in the Gulf of Mexico, and will cover an area of 500 square kilometers . SpaceX says it is working together with the authorities to protect the area's ecosystems, the coastline, wetlands, and wildlife , where the project will be located. The facilities will feature ten Starship launch pads , as well as maritime transport facilities and an airport .

Musk's envisioned AI data centers in space

Elon Musk has repeatedly outlined his technological projects that will be developed in space. The latest one is the creation of a satellite network to process Artificial Intelligence from space. In short, a data center outside Earth. The magnate proposes creating an orbital satellite network that would be even cheaper than conventional infrastructure due to lower electricity and cooling costs .

articles.title: Costco Gold Bars: How much they cost, where you can find them and why you should buy them
articles.standfirst: Costco has become an unexpected destination for precious-metals buyers
articles.summary: Costco has become an unexpected destination for precious-metals buyers
articles.body:
Gold bars are not necessarily the first product that comes to mind when thinking about a Costco shopping trip, but the warehouse retailer has built a surprisingly successful bullion business.

Demand for its precious metals has remained strong, with gold bars frequently selling out and Costco maintaining limits on how much individual members can purchase.

For shoppers considering a purchase, the biggest question is naturally the price. Costco's gold bars are generally sold at a relatively small premium over the underlying market price of gold rather than at the much larger markups sometimes charged by traditional dealers.

CNBC Select reports that Costco typically prices its gold at around 1% to 2% above the spot price, compared with markups that can reach 5% to 10% at some traditional gold dealers.

That means the exact amount changes frequently because the spot price of gold moves throughout the trading day.

As of September 14, 2026, Kitco reported a gold spot price of approximately $4,290.60 per troy ounce. Applying Costco's typical 1% to 2% premium would put the underlying retail cost at roughly $4,333 to $4,376, although the actual Costco listing can differ depending on the product and the live market price.

Where can you buy Costco gold bars?

Costco sells its bullion primarily through Costco.com, with gold also available at some U.S. warehouses depending on inventory and location.

The company sells one-troy-ounce, 24-karat bars from established refiners including PAMP Suisse and Rand Refinery.

The products are investment-grade bullion rather than jewelry. PAMP's popular Lady Fortuna bars and Rand Refinery's one-ounce bars contain high-purity gold and are supplied with assay documentation, giving buyers information that can help establish authenticity and specifications.

Availability, however, is one of the biggest challenges. Costco has previously said its one-ounce gold bars can sell out extremely quickly.

The retailer consequently introduced purchase restrictions, and CNBC currently reports a limit of one transaction per membership, with a maximum of four units within 24 hours.

Costco's Gold Star membership costs $65 annually, while an Executive membership costs $130. Those membership costs need to be considered when calculating the overall economics of buying bullion from the retailer.

There is another potential advantage for Executive members. Eligible Costco purchases can earn the Executive membership's 2% annual reward, while the Costco Anywhere Visa Card by Citi can provide additional cash back on eligible Costco purchases.

Why some investors like Costco's gold

The main attraction is the combination of a recognizable retailer and a comparatively low premium.

Gold investors normally pay more than the spot price when purchasing physical bullion because dealers have costs associated with refining, distribution and selling the metal. Costco's relatively narrow premium can reduce that initial hurdle.

Gold itself is also viewed by many investors as a diversification asset and potential safe haven during periods of economic or geopolitical uncertainty.

The metal has experienced extraordinary price movements in 2026, although that does not mean prices will continue rising. Reuters reported spot gold around $4,385 per ounce on September 8 after a recent decline, illustrating how quickly the market can move.

That volatility is important. Buying a Costco gold bar should not be treated as a guaranteed profit opportunity. Physical gold does not produce interest or dividends, and investors can lose money if the market price falls.

There are also practical disadvantages. Costco does not buy the gold back from customers, meaning sellers must find another dealer or buyer when they want to liquidate. Gold purchases are also non-refundable, and Costco does not provide storage for the bars.

That makes Costco potentially attractive for an investor who specifically wants to own physical gold and can safely store it, rather than someone simply looking for short-term exposure to gold prices.

Ultimately, the appeal of Costco's bullion is fairly straightforward: competitive premiums, established refiners, potential membership rewards and the convenience of buying through a familiar retailer.

But shoppers should compare the live Costco price with the current spot price before purchasing, factor in membership costs and rewards, and remember that physical gold carries storage and resale considerations that do not apply in the same way to gold ETFs.

For those comfortable with those trade-offs, Costco's gold bars offer an unusually accessible way to add physical precious metal to a broader investment strategy.

articles.summary: The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $251 million after Saturday's drawing produced no grand-prize winner, with a $106.6 million cash option available
articles.body:
The Powerball jackpot is back above the $250 million mark as players prepare for the Monday, September 14, 2026, drawing. The estimated top prize is $251 million, while the advertised cash option is $106.6 million before taxes.

Monday's winning numbers have not yet been drawn. The Powerball drawing is scheduled for 10:59 p.m. ET on Monday night, meaning the numbers cannot be confirmed earlier in the day.

Once the drawing takes place, players will be able to check the five white-ball numbers, the red Powerball and any applicable Power Play results through the official Powerball results service.

The jackpot reached $251 million after nobody matched all five white balls plus the Powerball during Saturday's September 12 drawing. The numbers drawn Saturday were 14, 16, 23, 58 and 69, with 3 as the Powerball and a 2X Power Play multiplier.

No ticket won the jackpot, while there were also no Match 5 winners for the standard $1 million second-tier prize.

That rollover increased the prize for Monday's drawing from the $232 million advertised for Saturday night to the current $251 million estimate. The corresponding cash value also moved from $100.2 million to $106.6 million.

What to know before the September 14 Powerball results

Powerball costs $2 per play, with players selecting five numbers from 1 through 69 and one red Powerball number from 1 through 26.

Players can choose their own numbers or use a terminal-generated Quick Pick. Power Play is an optional $1 addition that can increase most non-jackpot prizes.

The jackpot itself is won by matching all five white balls in any order and the red Powerball . There are nine ways to win a Powerball prize, so a ticket does not have to match every number to produce a payout.

The standard Match 5 prize is $1 million, while matching four white balls and the Powerball normally pays $50,000. Power Play can increase eligible non-jackpot prizes, with the Match 5 plus Power Play prize set at $2 million.

The size of the September 14 jackpot is also part of a steady sequence of rollovers. The prize was $173 million for the September 5 drawing, climbed to $190 million on September 7 and then reached $207 million on September 9.

Saturday's $232 million prize went unclaimed, producing the current $251 million estimate.

For someone who wins the jackpot, Powerball offers two payment structures. The winner can select the advertised annuity, which is paid through 30 graduated payments over 29 years, or take the one-time cash value. Both figures are stated before federal and applicable jurisdictional taxes.

The distinction between the two options is significant. Although the headline jackpot is $251 million, the immediate cash alternative is considerably smaller at $106.6 million.

A jackpot winner would also have to account for taxes when determining how much of the prize would ultimately remain available.

For now, however, the main question is whether Monday's drawing finally produces a jackpot winner.

Players should keep their tickets safe and check them carefully after the official drawing. Powerball drawings take place every Monday, Wednesday and Saturday at 10:59 p.m. ET, and official results should be used to verify winning numbers and prizes.

Once the September 14 balls are drawn, the winning combination will determine whether the $251 million jackpot is claimed or rolls over again for the next Powerball drawing.

articles.title: SNAP beneficiaries prepare for a September and October shake-up in their benefits
articles.standfirst: The food assistance program is undergoing changes that are already affecting beneficiaries.
articles.summary: The food assistance program is undergoing changes that are already affecting beneficiaries.
articles.body:
For millions of people who rely on SNAP to buy food , September brings uncertainty that could become even more significant in the coming weeks. The program is going through changes, and another shift is already prompting states to prepare for what comes next.

What is changing for SNAP beneficiaries?

Some of the changes are already tied to work requirements. The new legislation raised the maximum age from 54 to 64 for adults considered able to work and without dependents who must meet these requirements to keep SNAP benefits .

Some exemptions for parents and other family members responsible for caring for a dependent have also changed. In these cases, the age for qualifying under certain exemptions was lowered from 18 to 14 .

The impact is already beginning to be felt across the program. Nearly 5 million people have lost access to SNAP nationwide, including more than 1.5 million children , according to figures cited from the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities.

But the change that could shape the next chapter has yet to arrive.

Why could October be another key moment for SNAP?

Starting October 1, states will have to cover 75% of the administrative costs associated with operating SNAP . The change shifts a significant portion of the burden that had previously fallen on the federal government and is forcing states to prepare for higher expenses.

And that is not all. In the coming years, states are also expected to take on part of the cost of benefits based on their error rates. For most states, that additional obligation could range from 5% to 15%, depending on their performance .

But there is still a possibility of delaying the change. State and national organizations focused on food assistance are asking Congress to give states more time to prepare and lower their error rates .

And the timing matters: lawmakers return to Washington today, September 14 , with just over two weeks remaining before the new administrative cost-sharing structure takes effect.

The problem is that some states are already showing how difficult it could be to absorb the consequences.

That is where one of the biggest concerns comes in: food banks can help meet some of the need, but they do not have anything close to SNAP's capacity . In Arizona, a representative of the state's food bank network explained that for every meal these organizations are able to provide, SNAP typically provides around five.

With October approaching and states trying to prepare for the new costs, it remains to be seen whether Congress will allow the change to move forward on schedule or give states more time to adjust .

For people who rely on SNAP to buy food, that decision could ultimately be far more significant than an administrative change on paper.

articles.summary: The president’s return to Washington with Harp has reignited questions about the aide’s unusually close role
articles.body:
Donald Trump returned to the White House on Sunday night with one of his most closely watched aides, Natalie Harp , after a weekend in Ireland that once again placed their unusually close working relationship under the spotlight.

Harp , 35, traveled with the 80-year-old president during his two-day visit, which combined diplomatic meetings with a stop at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg for the Irish Open. Trump met Irish President Catherine Connolly and Taoiseach Micheál Martin before attending the tournament at his resort.

After the trip, Harp was photographed alongside Trump as they returned to Washington. She traveled aboard Air Force One and later Marine One, maintaining the proximity that has made her a familiar figure around the president.

First lady Melania Trump wasn't part of the delegation. Her absence attracted additional attention because of the limited number of public appearances she's made during Trump's second term.

During remarks in Dublin, Trump addressed his wife's absence with a joke, saying she was with him “in spirit” and was watching. He also said Melania had declined the lengthy flight after he invited her to join him.

“My wife is here in spirit. She’s watching right now,” Trump said. “I said, ‘Well, why don’t you come with me?’ She said, ‘Well, it’s a seven-hour trip. Maybe I’m not that friendly.’”

Harp’s unusual role keeps attracting attention

Harp's constant presence has generated considerable discussion in Washington. She has been nicknamed the “human printer” because she reportedly carries a portable printer and supplies Trump with printed news reports, social-media posts and other material.

Her role has made her a distinctive figure among the president's aides, particularly because of the reportedly personal nature of some of her interactions with him.

Reports have also focused on personal notes Harp allegedly left for Trump , intensifying questions about the boundaries of their professional relationship.

Trump has reportedly praised her loyalty, while the White House has repeatedly rejected suggestions that their relationship is inappropriate.

The scrutiny grew again during the Ireland trip after journalist Aaron Rupar highlighted Harp's presence online. The White House's Rapid Response 47 account responded with a personal attack on Rupar , accusing him of posting “creepy” material about the president and his staff.

The exchange shows the increasingly combative relationship between the Trump administration and members of the media who scrutinize the president and those around him.

Harp has largely avoided public comment throughout the controversy. Her continued presence beside Trump means that she remains a prominent subject of attention whenever the president travels.

Melania's absence has added another layer to that attention, although representatives for the first lady have pushed back against speculation about her private life or relationship with Harp , as the White House maintains that Harp's role is strictly professional.

As Trump continues his second term, Harp's proximity to the president is likely to remain a topic of interest, particularly whenever she appears alongside him on high-profile domestic or international trips.

articles.title: SSDI Payment September 2026: Who will be getting their disability benefits tomorrow for this month?
articles.standfirst: The next September disability payment is going to beneficiaries in one specific birthday group
articles.summary: The next September disability payment is going to beneficiaries in one specific birthday group
articles.body:
Millions of Americans rely on Social Security Disability Insurance each month, but their payments do not all arrive on the same day.

The next September 2026 SSDI payment is scheduled for Wednesday, September 16, and it applies primarily to beneficiaries whose birthdays fall between the 11th and 20th of any month.

Social Security uses a staggered payment system for most retirement and disability beneficiaries.

Under that schedule, people born between the 1st and 10th are generally paid on the second Wednesday of the month, those born between the 11th and 20th on the third Wednesday, and those born between the 21st and 31st on the fourth Wednesday.

In September, that places the three regular Wednesday payment dates on Sept. 9, Sept. 16 and Sept. 23. The official 2026 calendar confirms that Sept. 16 is the third Wednesday of the month.

Who should expect an SSDI payment on September 16?

The September 16 payment is generally for SSDI recipients with birthdays from the 11th through the 20th who follow the standard birthday-based schedule.

That means a beneficiary born on January 15, May 11 or October 20 would normally fall into Wednesday's payment group. Some beneficiaries are paid on a different schedule, however.

People who began receiving Social Security before May 1997, as well as many people who receive both Supplemental Security Income and Social Security benefits, are generally paid their Social Security benefit on the third day of the month instead.

The same birthday rule also applies when certain family or survivor benefits are based on another worker's earnings record. In those cases, the payment date is tied to the birthday of the person whose record the benefit is based on.

When is the final September SSDI payment?

Beneficiaries who are not due money on September 16 may still have another payment date coming later in the month. The final regular September payment is scheduled for Wednesday, Sept. 23, for recipients whose birthdays fall between the 21st and 31st.

Most Social Security benefits are delivered electronically through direct deposit or a Direct Express debit card. Anyone who does not receive an expected payment should first check with their bank or financial institution in case the deposit has been delayed on that end.

The Social Security Administration 's 2026 schedule also advises beneficiaries to allow three additional mailing days before contacting the agency about a missing payment.

articles.title: Maya Angelou, American author: "Success is liking yourself, liking what you do, and liking how you do it"
articles.standfirst: The acclaimed author believed achievement starts with self-respect rather than money, status or recognition
articles.summary: The acclaimed author believed achievement starts with self-respect rather than money, status or recognition
articles.body:
Success is often treated as something visible: a bigger salary, a better title, public recognition or evidence that a person has risen above everyone around them. Maya Angelou offered a much more demanding definition.

“Success is liking yourself, liking what you do, and liking how you do it,” the celebrated American author, poet and civil rights activist said in a quote that has endured because of its simplicity.

Angelou ’s words shift the measure of achievement away from what other people can see. Her definition asks whether a person is comfortable with who they have become, whether they find meaning in the work that fills their days and whether they can respect the choices they made getting there.

That perspective was especially striking coming from someone whose own life produced no shortage of conventional accomplishments.

Angelou published seven autobiographies, multiple essay collections and numerous volumes of poetry, while also working across theater, film and television.

Her 1969 memoir, I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings , brought her international recognition and established her as one of the most important literary voices of her generation.

Her definition of success was more complicated

Her rise was anything but straightforward. Before becoming famous as a writer, Angelou worked a wide variety of jobs, including as a cook, nightclub performer and cast member in Porgy and Bess.

She later worked as a journalist in Egypt and Ghana and became deeply involved in the Civil Rights Movement.

She worked with both Martin Luther King Jr. and Malcolm X , experiences that placed questions of dignity, identity and moral conviction at the center of her public life.

Angelou ’s writing repeatedly examined race, trauma, family and identity, often asking what it takes to build a sense of self in a world that may try to define a person from the outside. Her idea of success therefore begins internally rather than with approval.

Questions of character and method are introduced in her ideas. Achievement alone isn't enough if reaching it requires behavior a person cannot respect afterward.

Angelou ’s own public career continued well beyond her literary breakthrough. She became the Reynolds Professor of American Studies at Wake Forest University in 1982 and remained a prominent lecturer into her eighties.

In 1993, she delivered “On the Pulse of Morning” at Bill Clinton ’s first presidential inauguration, becoming the first poet to give an inaugural recitation since Robert Frost at John F. Kennedy ’s inauguration in 1961.

Angelou accumulated honors, awards and more than 50 honorary degrees.

articles.title: Will the IRS be knocking on your door? This is who might get an IRS visit pretty soon
articles.standfirst: Revenue Officers can visit homes and businesses across the country, but a visit does not automatically mean seizure
articles.summary: Revenue Officers can visit homes and businesses across the country, but a visit does not automatically mean seizure
articles.body:
Most taxpayers who owe money to the IRS will never have a federal employee unexpectedly appear at their home or business. But in some unresolved cases, the agency can still move beyond letters and phone calls and arrange an in-person meeting.

Those cases are generally handled by Revenue Officers, IRS employees responsible for collecting unpaid federal taxes and addressing required returns that haven't been filed.

Their involvement usually comes after the agency has already tried to make contact.

A taxpayer who has ignored repeated notices, has a significant unresolved balance or has failed to file required returns may eventually have a Revenue Officer assigned to the case.

That doesn't mean the IRS is launching a special campaign in Los Angeles, Miami, Dallas, New York, Chicago or any other city. The same collection authority applies nationwide.

Most IRS visits now arranged before anyone arrives

The IRS changed its approach to field visits in 2023, ending most unannounced Revenue Officer visits.

The agency now generally contacts taxpayers in advance and may use Letter 725-B to schedule an appointment. Depending on the circumstances, that meeting can take place at an IRS office, a home or business, or by phone.

That shift was designed in part to reduce confusion caused by scammers impersonating government employees and to make encounters safer for both taxpayers and IRS staff. There are still exceptions.

Unscheduled visits can occur in a narrower range of enforcement situations, including some cases involving summonses, seizures or other actions where advance notice may not be appropriate. Those visits aren't considered routine.

A visit doesn't mean the IRS is about to seize your property

The appearance of a Revenue Officer can understandably feel serious, but it does not automatically mean a taxpayer is about to lose a bank account, vehicle or home.

The officer may first review the debt, determine what returns remain outstanding and explain available ways to resolve the account. Depending on the taxpayer’s financial situation, that can include installment agreements or other collection alternatives.

More aggressive action can follow if the debt remains unresolved and the IRS completes the required legal steps. Those measures can include a federal tax lien, a levy on funds or, in more limited circumstances, seizure of assets.

The process typically involves multiple notices and opportunities to respond before reaching that stage.

How to verify someone claiming to be from IRS

Anyone receiving an in-person visit should verify the employee’s identity before sharing information or making a payment.

Revenue Officers and Revenue Agents carry official government credentials, including identification with a photograph and serial number. IRS Criminal Investigation Special Agents carry law-enforcement credentials.

Taxpayers should be especially cautious if someone demands immediate payment, refuses to provide identification or pressures them to hand over sensitive financial information.

IRS visits still happen, but most are neither random nor unexpected. They are generally the result of a tax problem that has remained unresolved long enough to require direct contact.

articles.title: Bill Gates, investor, and philanthropist: ”I never took a day off in my 20s. Not one"
articles.standfirst: Gates’ relentless approach helped shape Microsoft
articles.summary: Gates’ relentless approach helped shape Microsoft
articles.body:
Bill Gates built Microsoft during a period when personal computing was still finding its place in everyday life, and his approach to those early years was anything but casual.

“I never took a day off in my 20s. Not one,” Gates once said, a remark that has since become one of the clearest summaries of the intensity that defined the first stage of his career.

The quote is often repeated as evidence of the work ethic behind one of the most successful technology companies in history. Yet it also raises a more complicated question about how much of a person’s life should be sacrificed in pursuit of a goal.

Gates co-founded Microsoft with Paul Allen in 1975, when he was still only 19. Through his twenties, the company expanded rapidly as software became central to the emerging personal computer market. That period demanded almost total focus.

Culture that shaped Microsoft rise

The striking part of Gates ’ statement isn't simply that he worked hard. It's the absoluteness of it. A level of commitment far removed from the conventional idea of balancing work with weekends, vacations or extended breaks.

That mentality became closely associated with Silicon Valley’s early entrepreneurial culture, where founders were often expected to treat their companies as all-consuming missions.

Gates ’ own career helps explain why he adopted that mindset. Microsoft was competing in a fast-changing industry, and the opportunities available to software companies were expanding quickly. The result was extraordinary.

Microsoft grew into one of the dominant companies of the personal-computing era, while Gates became one of the most recognizable business figures in the world.

Gates became ‘a little less fanatical’

Years later, Gates added important context to the way he viewed that period of his life. “And I’m still fanatical, but now I’m a little less fanatical,” he said.

It suggests Gates still valued discipline and deep commitment, but no longer believed the level of intensity he maintained in his twenties had to continue indefinitely.

His life gradually broadened beyond Microsoft as well. Gates stepped away from the company’s day-to-day leadership and devoted increasing attention to philanthropy, global health and other projects through the Gates Foundation .

He also spoke more openly about making time for family and personal interests. The quote remains powerful because it shows what obsession can help build.

His later perspective is just as revealing because it suggests that even one of the world’s most driven entrepreneurs eventually decided there was value in becoming “a little less fanatical.”

articles.title: What is the Super El Niño 2026 Forecast and which states will be most affected?
articles.standfirst: California, Texas and the Southeast may turn stormier while much of the northern U.S. faces a milder winter
articles.summary: California, Texas and the Southeast may turn stormier while much of the northern U.S. faces a milder winter
articles.body:
The weather pattern reshaping conditions across the Pacific is entering a more consequential phase, with NOAA now warning that El Niño is strengthening rapidly ahead of the 2026-27 winter.

The Climate Prediction Center said in its September 10 update that there is a greater than 90% chance of a very strong El Niño through the Northern Hemisphere fall and winter.

Sea-surface temperature anomalies in the key Niño 3.4 region had climbed to around 1.8 degrees Celsius above normal in August, while even larger anomalies were recorded farther east.

A very strong event is sometimes informally described as a “Super El Niño.” The label doesn't mean every affected area will experience extreme weather, but stronger events generally increase the odds that familiar El Niño patterns will emerge.

That could make the next several months particularly important across the United States.

Southern states face clearest signal for wetter winter

El Niño changes the atmosphere by warming the tropical Pacific and shifting the jet stream southward.

NOAA says that shift typically directs more winter storms across the southern United States, increasing the chances of wetter and sometimes cooler conditions from California through the Gulf Coast and into parts of the Southeast.

That puts California, Arizona, New Mexico, Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia and Florida among the states most likely to experience noticeable changes if the traditional pattern develops.

California can face repeated Pacific storms during strong El Niño winters, while Texas and the Gulf Coast can see increased rainfall.

The Southeast, including Florida , also tends to be wetter than normal, potentially increasing flood risks where storms repeatedly track through the same areas.

Still, NOAA cautions against treating those tendencies as guarantees.

“Every El Niño is not the same; each one is unique with its own imprint on our weather,” National Weather Service Director Ken Graham said when the event developed earlier this year.

Northern states could see opposite effect

The northern half of the country often experiences a very different winter during El Niño .

The Pacific Northwest, northern Rockies, northern Plains and Great Lakes typically tilt warmer and, in several areas, drier than average because the main storm track shifts south.

States including Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Montana, North Dakota, Minnesota, Wisconsin and Michigan could therefore see fewer prolonged cold outbreaks and less storminess than they would during a typical winter.

The Mountain West is less straightforward. Utah and Colorado can sit near the dividing line between the wetter southern storm track and drier northern pattern, making snowfall outcomes particularly dependent on exactly where individual systems travel.

El Niño usually exerts its strongest influence on U.S. weather during winter, meaning its most significant effects may still be months away.

What is already clear is that this is no ordinary event. The stronger it becomes, the greater the chance that millions of Americans will notice its fingerprints on the winter ahead.

articles.title: Helicopter explodes into flames near LA bus crash, leaving at least 3 dead in horrific scene
articles.standfirst: A news helicopter crashed and burst into flames in Los Angeles while covering another deadly accident, leaving at least three people dead.
articles.summary: A news helicopter crashed and burst into flames in Los Angeles while covering another deadly accident, leaving at least three people dead.
articles.body:
A news helicopter crashed in a Los Angeles neighborhood Tuesday night and burst into flames, leaving at least three people dead near the scene of an earlier crash involving an SUV and a city bus, authorities said.

The helicopter went down around 7 p.m. near a one-story commercial building in Chatsworth , in the San Fernando Valley, while news crews were covering the bus accident that had already claimed at least two lives and left six others injured, according to the Los Angeles Fire Department .

An anchor for NBC4 Los Angeles confirmed during a live broadcast that the station’s helicopter crashed shortly before 7 p.m.

Los Angeles Fire Department spokesperson Capt. Branden Silverman said at least one person killed in the helicopter crash was found outside the aircraft, in a parking lot next to the commercial building. It remained unclear whether the other two victims were inside the helicopter or on the ground.

One person was transported to a hospital, though their condition was not immediately known.

“We’re trying to determine how many patients were inside the helicopter,” Silverman said, describing the aircraft as “pretty well destroyed.” Authorities said crews would search through the wreckage to determine how many people were on board.

The crash also sparked a fire that damaged at least four vehicles and two storage containers on the ground. The flames were quickly extinguished, with more than 50 firefighters responding to the scene.

The helicopter crash occurred about two hours after an SUV slammed into the side of a city bus in Chatsworth, killing at least two people and injuring six others. Images shared online showed the front half of the SUV embedded into the side of an MTA bus .

The two crashes occurred about 1.5 miles apart .

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) will investigate the cause of the helicopter crash.

The crash also sparked a fire that damaged at least four vehicles and two storage containers on the ground. The flames were quickly extinguished, with more than 50 firefighters responding to the scene.

The helicopter crash occurred about two hours after an SUV slammed into the side of a city bus in Chatsworth, killing at least two people and injuring six others. Images shared online showed the front half of the SUV embedded into the side of an MTA bus .
The two crashes occurred about 1.5 miles apart .
The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) will investigate the cause of the helicopter crash.

articles.title: “In 1970, Washington tied thousands of discarded tires to reefs to improve bottom fishing: years later, the ropes failed and 100,000 remained submerged”
articles.standfirst: A study reveals how these artificial habitats create unforeseen problems
articles.summary: A study reveals how these artificial habitats create unforeseen problems
articles.body:
When nature is not suited to human development, humans seek ways to shape it artificially for their own interest and development as a society, without being aware of what this means for the environment.

In Washington, they decided in the 1970s that it would be a good idea to create artificial reefs in Puget Sound to improve the seabed for fish such as rock cod and expand recreational fishing opportunities. To do this, they dumped more than 100,000 discarded tires tied together with polypropylene rope into the water, distributed across 20 locations in the area.

Now, nearly 40 years later, this case was studied by the University of Washington's School of Marine and Environmental Affairs, which offers a clear conclusion: creating artificial marine habitats can generate serious problems.

Promoting creative fishing: the reason behind the more than 100,000 tires submerged in Washington

According to the university, at that time, the laws were quite strict regarding salmon fishing, which led sport fishermen to focus on bottom fishing for species such as rockfish. The state's Department of Fish and Wildlife even came to collaborate with fishing groups to carry out this project.

The problem was not only that tires were used, but also that they incorporated concrete, plastics, PVC, and even train cars. With all of this, reefs were formed so that small fish could use them as shelter. Everything seemed perfect until the polypropylene rope that held the tires together deteriorated and allowed these objects to move from their original locations and spread across the seabed. Some even reached the coast.

More than 100,000 tires are still being collected from the seabed

According to a KING report, it is estimated that more than 100,000 tires remain in Puget Sound, but the figure is believed to be higher. Now, the Department of Natural Resources is working to locate the piles of tires, recover them from the water, and send the damaged material for proper disposal.

articles.title: Who was Eliana Moreno? The NBC and Telemundo reporter killed in Los Angeles helicopter crash
articles.standfirst: The Chapman graduate spent more than a decade covering wildfires, traffic incidents and breaking news from NewsChopper4
articles.summary: The Chapman graduate spent more than a decade covering wildfires, traffic incidents and breaking news from NewsChopper4
articles.body:
Eliana Moreno spent years doing the kind of journalism that put her directly above unfolding emergencies, giving viewers a perspective few reporters could provide from the ground.

That work ended Tuesday night when the helicopter carrying Moreno and pilot George Marciniw crashed in Chatsworth while covering a serious traffic collision involving a Metro bus.

NBC4 and Telemundo 52 confirmed that Moreno , a longtime aerial photographer and reporter with Angel City Air , was aboard NewsChopper4 when it went down shortly before 7 p.m. in the 9100 block of North Mason Avenue.

Marciniw was also killed, along with a person on the ground. Two others were taken to the hospital. The cause of the crash remains under investigation.

Moreno always wanted to be a reporter

Moreno was born in Orange County and graduated from Chapman University in 2010 with degrees in broadcast journalism and political science. She had known from an early age what she wanted to do.

Before joining Angel City Air in September 2010, Moreno worked for several Orange County media outlets in both Spanish and English. Her background included reporting, anchoring, producing and camera work.

She was also fluent in Spanish and regularly spoke with students interested in journalism. Her career eventually became closely associated with aerial reporting, particularly during wildfires and fast-moving breaking-news events.

More than dramatic pictures

Moreno ’s role in NewsChopper4 centered on giving viewers useful real-time information from the air. Moreno also provided essential coverage of brushfires and how firefighters were working to contain them.

That type of reporting became a major part of her professional identity. Moreno and Marciniw had reportedly been flying together since 2023.

NBC4 and Telemundo 52 said in a joint statement: “We are deeply saddened to share that a helicopter providing aerial news coverage for NBC4 and Telemundo 52 was involved in a fatal accident in Los Angeles on Tuesday evening.

“We extend our heartfelt condolences to the families, friends and colleagues of those who lost their lives.”

The National Transportation Safety Board said it is investigating the September 15 crash involving a Eurocopter AS350 B2, with federal investigators expected at the scene Wednesday.

Moreno ’s death came while she was doing the work she had spent years building her career around: helping viewers understand a developing emergency from the air.
